prompt: How many events does the record hold?
How many tool calls use the tool "Bash"?
How many tool results have status "error"?
How many distinct file paths (the args field "file_path") appear in tool calls of the tools "Edit" or "Write"?
How many user messages contain "test" in their text, case-insensitively? Any occurrence of the four letters counts, so "tests" counts.
For each tool, the number of tool calls using it. Columns: tool, calls. Order: calls descending, then tool ascending.

The three runs with the most assistant-message tokens: the sum of tokens over assistant messages only, not tool calls. Columns: run, tokens. Order: tokens descending, then run ascending. Exactly three rows.

For each tool that has at least one tool result: the number of its tool results with status "error", the number of all its tool results, and their ratio errors / results as a float. Columns: tool, errors, results, rate. Order: rate descending, then tool ascending.
For every run, the number of compaction events (kind "compaction") in it, including runs that have none. Columns: run, compactions. Order: run ascending.
The five files read most often, counting the args field "file_path" of tool calls of the tool "Read". Columns: file_path, reads. Order: reads descending, then file_path ascending. Exactly five rows.
For each writer: the number of its events and its highest seq. Columns: writer, events, max_seq. Order: writer ascending.

For each tool, the average duration in seconds of its tool calls that have a tool result. A call's duration is its result's ts minus the call's ts, matched by call_id. Columns: tool, avg_seconds (a float). Order: tool ascending.
How many tool calls have no tool result with the same call_id?
The call_id of the tool call with the longest duration, with duration as in: result ts minus call ts, matched by call_id, for calls that have a result. If several tie, the smallest call_id.

For each Bash command (the args field "command" of tool calls of the tool "Bash") that failed at least once, meaning at least one of its calls has a result with status "error": the number of Bash calls with that command, whether or not they have a result, and the number of those calls whose result has status "error". Columns: command, runs, failures. Order: failures descending, then command ascending.
Count the tool calls of the tool "Edit" whose args "file_path" was not the args "file_path" of any tool call of the tool "Read" earlier in the same writer (lower seq).
Count the user messages per hour of the day in UTC (0 to 23), taken from ts. Columns: hour (an integer), messages. Only hours with at least one user message. Order: hour ascending.
For each run, its span: the largest ts minus the smallest ts among its events. Columns: run, span. Order: span descending, then run ascending.
On how many distinct UTC calendar days was there at least one user message? A day is ts divided by 86400, rounded down.

The largest gap in ts between two consecutive events of the same writer, where consecutive means adjacent in seq order. Columns: writer, seq (the seq of the later event of the pair), gap (in seconds). If several gaps tie, take the smallest writer, then the smallest seq. Exactly one row.
The sum of the args field "pre_tokens" over compaction events whose args field "trigger" is "auto".
Tool results of the tool "Bash" with status "error" have text such as "command failed: exit code 2". Count them per exit code. Columns: code (an integer), results. Order: code ascending.
The recall queries (the args field "query" of events of kind "recall") that occur more than once, each listed once, in ascending order.

For tool calls of the tool "Edit", count the edits per file extension: the text after the last "." in the args field "file_path", without the dot. Columns: ext, edits. Order: edits descending, then ext ascending.

Walk each writer's tool results in seq order. Find the longest run of consecutive tool results that all have status "error", with no "ok" tool result between them; events of other kinds do not break a run. Return the length of the longest such run across all writers.

Split each run's events, in seq order, into sessions: a session starts at the run's first event and at every event whose ts is more than 1800 seconds after the ts of the run's previous event. How many sessions are there across all runs?

Replay the events of kind "pin" in writer then seq order. An event whose args field "action" is "add" makes the pin named by its args field "pin_id" active; "remove" makes it inactive. List the pin_ids active at the end, in plain ascending string order.

A turn starts at a user message and holds every event of the same writer from it up to, not including, that writer's next user message. For each run, count its turns that hold at least one tool result with status "error". Columns: run, turns. Leave out runs with no such turn. Order: run ascending.

A retry is a tool call whose previous tool call in the same writer (the tool call with the next lower seq) has the same tool and exactly the same args text, and has a tool result with status "error". How many retries are there?

For each run, walk its events in seq order keeping a running sum of tokens. Report the seq of the first event at which the running sum reaches 50000 or more. Columns: run, seq. Leave out runs that never reach it. Order: run ascending.
